about: Hiruzta, meaning “a harvest of three,” is the family winery of Asensio Rekalde and his sons Txarli and Ángel in Hondarribia, the Basque border town at the mouth of the Bidasoa. Hondarribia gave its name to the region’s two native grapes, Hondarrabi Zuri (white) and Hondarrabi Beltza (red). Local txakoli-making was lost for centuries after the sieges of the 1600s, and the Rekaldes revived it in the late 2000s on the slopes of Mount Jaizkibel.

The rosé is 60% Hondarrabi Beltza and 40% Hondarrabi Zuri from the 11-hectare estate around the winery. The vines face the midday sun and are sheltered from the sea’s wind and damp. The grapes are picked by hand, destemmed and crushed. The red juice sits on its skins for just four to six hours in the cold before it is drawn off, then blended with white Hondarrabi Zuri juice and fermented at 16–18°C. In 2024 a warm, dry spring brought budbreak almost a month early, but a cool summer slowed ripening to a normal harvest date.

The winery describes a redcurrant-pink wine with strawberry, blackberry and blackcurrant over citrus and a fine vegetal note. The palate is fresh and lifted by a light prickle of natural carbon dioxide, with balanced acidity and a long, aromatic finish. The winery recommends serving it at 8–10°C with shellfish, rice dishes, cured meats or mild cheeses, and drinking it within about two years of the vintage.
facts: 4–6 hour cold skin contact and bleed (saignée), blended with white juice; fermented at 16–18°C
11 ha estate below Mount Jaizkibel; clay marl over bedrock; double Guyot
Dry rosé with a light natural spritz
